claims.text: Between 14 and 18 August the site published seven vaults, each a real encrypted vault openable in a browser from a read key printed on its page.
claims.quote: Between 14 and 18 August this site published seven vaults.

claims.text: By the seventh vault there was a method, and every rule in it exists because something went wrong first.
claims.quote: By the seventh there was a method, and every rule in it exists because something went wrong first.

claims.text: The rule that matters most: classify the credential before it touches anything.
claims.quote: Classify the credential before it touches anything.

claims.text: Three of the seven vaults arrived as a vault key described as a read key, and a vault key is write access.
claims.quote: Three of the seven vaults arrived as a vault key described as a read key. A vault key is write access.

value.unit: vaults submitted with a write credential described as a read key

claims.text: Because a vault key is also the address and the encryption root, publishing one would be unrecoverable: no revocation, no rotation, and no undo.
claims.quote: because a vault key is also the address and the encryption root, there is no revocation, no rotation, and no undo.

claims.text: The write credentials were caught by shape: a read key is 64 hex characters, a vault key is a generated passphrase of 24 lowercase alphanumerics.
claims.quote: A read key is 64 hex characters; a vault key is a generated passphrase, which is 24 lowercase alphanumerics.

claims.text: A catch that depended on somebody looking is not a control, so it became a script that exits 0 for publishable and 1 for stop, and never echoes what it was given.
claims.quote: That catch depended on somebody looking, which is not a control.

claims.text: Behind the script the release validator scans every tracked file for any key-shaped string and for the actual passphrases, read at build time from a gitignored tier.
claims.quote: the release validator scans every tracked file for any key-shaped string and for the actual passphrases, read at build time from a gitignored tier.

claims.text: The tripwire has caught its own author three times, each time writing the prefix in prose; a rule that only catches other people is not a rule.
claims.quote: That tripwire has caught its own author three times, each time writing the prefix in prose

value.unit: times the tripwire caught its own author

claims.text: A read key is derived one-way from a vault key, so a submission that cannot be published can still become one that can; the vault key goes to the gitignored tier and the derived read key is published.
claims.quote: A read key is derived one-way from a vault key, so a submission that cannot be published can still become one that can

claims.text: The whole shape of the project is a capability you can hand over that is strictly less than the one you hold, with the reduction enforced by mathematics rather than by policy.
claims.quote: a capability you can hand over that is strictly less than the one you hold, with the reduction enforced by mathematics rather than by policy.

claims.text: Audit with exactly the credential a reader will have, across every file, not with the vault key.
claims.quote: With exactly the credential a reader will have, across every file.

claims.text: One vault carried a sealed LLM credential; the published read key was used to attempt to open it, AES-GCM refused with InvalidTag, so no budget was exposed.
claims.quote: AES-GCM refused, InvalidTag, so no budget was exposed.

claims.text: The rule of no metered capability behind a published read key came from the sixth vault, Risk Graph Explorer, the first public by design, and was adopted into the guidance.
claims.quote: the third, no metered capability behind a published read key, was not in our guidance. It is now.

claims.text: Every screenshot on a vault page is taken by opening the actual vault in a real browser with the published read key, performing the navigation and cropping; no mock-ups.
claims.quote: Every screenshot on a vault page is taken by opening the actual vault in a real browser with the published read key, performing the navigation, and cropping the result. No mock-ups.

claims.text: Every vault page ends with what the vault does not do, as a section with the same weight as the features; an argument that omits its own edges is a brochure.
claims.quote: an argument that omits its own edges is a brochure.

claims.text: Seven vaults took roughly four days of work, and the method is written down as a playbook aimed at another site's agent.
claims.quote: Seven vaults, roughly four days of work

value.unit: days of work for seven vaults

claims.text: Three bugs were found by testing rather than assumption on a single page, a malformed selector, leaking escape sequences and an unloaded component, and all three would have shipped.
claims.quote: Three bugs found by testing rather than assumption on a single page

value.unit: bugs found by testing on one page

claims.text: The seven vaults span the range deliberately, from one that requests no permissions at all to one that can write a single folder.
claims.quote: The seven vaults span the range deliberately, from one that requests no permissions at all to one that can write a single folder.
